GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2016-02-16T08:42:14Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: flatMapIterable and toList combination issue
Description: In the following code the "three" and "done" never appears in the output. Looks like the problem is in `toList` call. Am i using it wrong?

```
PublishSubject<Boolean> mBooleanPublishSubject = PublishSubject.create();
Observable<Boolean> observable = mBooleanPublishSubject.asObservable().share();
observable
        .doOnNext(__ -> System.out.println("one"))
        .flatMap(__ -> Observable.just(Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3, 4)))
        .flatMapIterable(number -> number)
        .doOnNext(v -> System.out.println("two " + v))
        .toList()
        .doOnNext(v -> System.out.println("three " + v))
        .subscribe(v -> System.out.println("done"));
mBooleanPublishSubject.onNext(true);
```


You must provide a category number (1-3). Your response must follow this format exactly:

CATEGORY: [category number]
REASONING: [your reasoning here, including specific reasons why an issue would be hard to dockerize if choosing category 3]
llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is a conceptual problem with RxJava operators that can be analyzed without needing to build or run the code. The issue is that `toList()` collects all items and emits them as a single list when the source Observable completes, but in this case, the `PublishSubject` never completes (no `onComplete()` is called). Therefore, the operators after `toList()` never execute because they're waiting for completion. This is a common RxJava behavior that can be verified through code analysis without needing to set up a build environment. The solution would be to either call `onComplete()` on the subject or use operators like `take()` or `buffer()` instead of `toList()` if completion isn't desired. This is purely a conceptual understanding of how RxJava operators work.
